page: Hetzner Cloud cpx32 is an x86_64 server powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. It features 4 virtual CPUs (vCPUs) mapped to 4 physical cores with a shared CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of RAM, providing approximately 1.95 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 160 GB NVMe SSD. The hypervisor layer is managed via QEMU.

In benchmark testing, the cpx32 demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 3040.68, placing it in the top 25%. Multi-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 12106.51 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 6029.0. Memory write bandwidth for large blocks is strong at 105.43 GB/sec, while read bandwidth remains average. Static web serving throughput is a relative bottleneck, registering at 4.05 GB/sec, which falls into the bottom 25%.

Due to its shared CPU allocation, the cpx32 is appropriate for workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated CPU performance. It is configured for software compilation, basic database operations, and lightweight text or image processing. The instance also supports basic machine learning tasks, achieving 219.62 tokens per second for text generation on a small 135M LLM, though performance drops significantly on larger models. It represents a cost-efficient entry point for development environments, CI/CD pipelines, and utility servers where resource density and NVMe storage are prioritized over dedicated CPU guarantees.
description: Hetzner Cloud cpx32 is an x86_64 virtual server configured with 4 shared AMD EPYC vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz and 8.0 GB of RAM. It includes 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and operates under a QEMU hypervisor. Performance benchmarks show strong single-core CPU capabilities and high large-block memory write bandwidth, though multi-core execution and static web serving throughput remain average to weak. The shared CPU allocation makes this instance a cost-effective option for workloads with variable CPU demands. It is recommended for software compilation, development environments, lightweight database operations, and utility services that benefit from fast local storage without requiring dedicated CPU cores.
